title: 2024年考研英语一 Part B · 信息匹配

sentences: Directions; Read the following comments on a report about American museums returning artifacts to their countries of origin and a list of statements summarizing the comments.
Choose the best statement from the list A—G for each numbered name (41— 45).
There are two extra choices which you do not need to use.
Mark your answers on the ANSWER SHEET.
(10 points)
translations: 说明；阅读以下关于美国博物馆将文物归还其原产国的报告的评论，以及总结这些评论的陈述列表。
从列表A—G中为每个编号的名字（41—45）选择最佳陈述。
有两个额外选项你不需要使用。
在答题卡上标记你的答案。

sentences: (41) Hannah Simply, there are people in Nigeria who cannot travel to the Smithsonian Institution to see that part of their history and culture represented by the Benin Bronzes.
These should be available to them as part of their cultural heritage and history and as a source of national pride.
There is no good reason that these artifacts should be beyond the ordinary reach of the educational objectives or inspiration of the generations to which they were left.
They serve no purpose in a museum in the United States or elsewhere except as curious objects.
They cannot be compared to works of art produced for sale which can be passed from hand to hand and place to place by purchase.
translations: (41) 汉娜 简单地说，尼日利亚有些人无法前往史密森尼学会观看贝宁青铜器所代表的他们历史和文化的那个部分。
这些应该作为他们文化遗产和历史的一部分，以及民族自豪感的来源，提供给他们。
没有充分理由认为这些文物应该超出它们所留给后代的教育目标或灵感的普通范围。
它们在美国或其他地方的博物馆中除了作为奇特的物品外，没有任何用途。
它们不能与为销售而生产的艺术品相比，后者可以通过购买从一手传到另一手，从一个地方传到另一个地方。

sentences: (42) Buck We know very exact reproductions of artwork can be and are regularly produced.
Perhaps museums and governments might explore some role for the use of nearly exact reproductions as a means of resolving issues relating to returning works of art and antiquities.
The context of any exhibit is more important to me than whether the object being displayed is 2,000 years old or 2 months old.
In many cases the experts have a hard time agreeing on what is the real object and what is a forgery.
Again, the story an exhibit is trying to tell is what matters.
The monetary value of the objects on display is a distant second place in importance.
translations: (42) 巴克 我们知道非常精确的艺术品复制品可以并且经常被生产出来。
也许博物馆和政府可以探索使用几乎精确的复制品作为解决与归还艺术品和古物相关的问题的一种手段的某种作用。
对我来说，任何展览的背景比展示的物品是2000年前还是2个月前更重要。
在许多情况下，专家们很难就什么是真实物品和什么是赝品达成一致。
再次，展览试图讲述的故事才是重要的。
展示物品的货币价值在重要性上远远排在第二位。

sentences: (43) Sara When visiting the Baltimore Museum of Art, I came across a magnificent 15th-century Chinese sculpture.
It inspired me to learn more about the culture that it represented.
Artifacts in museums have the power to inspire, and perhaps spark that need to learn and understand the nature of their creators.
Having said that, I do feel that whatever artifacts find their way to public museums should, in fact, be sanctioned as having been obtained on loan, legally purchased, or obtained by treaty.
Stealing artifacts from other peoples’ cultures is obscene; it robs not only the physical objects, but the dignity and spirit of their creators.
translations: (43) 萨拉 在参观巴尔的摩艺术博物馆时，我偶然看到一件宏伟的15世纪中国雕塑。
它激励我更多地了解它所代表的文化。
博物馆中的文物具有激励的力量，也许能激发学习和理解其创作者本质的需求。
话虽如此，我确实觉得任何进入公共博物馆的文物都应该被批准为通过借展、合法购买或通过条约获得。
从其他民族的文化中偷窃文物是令人憎恶的；它不仅剥夺了实物，还剥夺了其创作者的尊严和精神。

sentences: (44) Victor Ancient art that is displayed in foreign countries by all means should be returned to the original country.
The foreign countries have no right to hold back returning the items.
I would ask that the foreign nations and the original country discuss the terms of transfer.
Yes, there is the risk that the original country will not have as good security as do the foreign countries.
But look at what happened to Boston’s Gardner Museum theft in 1990, including the loss of Rembrandt, Vermeer, Manet, and other masterpieces.
Nothing is absolutely safe, nowhere.
And now Climate Change agitators are attacking publicly displayed works in European museums.
translations: (44) 维克多 在国外展示的古代艺术无论如何都应该归还给原产国。
外国无权阻止归还这些物品。
我会要求外国和原产国讨论转让条款。
是的，存在原产国的安全措施不如外国好的风险。
但看看1990年波士顿加德纳博物馆盗窃案发生了什么，包括丢失了伦勃朗、维米尔、马奈和其他杰作。
没有什么是绝对安全的，任何地方都没有。
而现在气候变化煽动者正在攻击欧洲博物馆公开展示的作品。

sentences: (45) Julia To those of you in the comments section who are having strong feelings about artifacts being removed from cities in the US and Britain and returned to their countries of origin, I would ask you to consider: why do you think Americans have more of a right to easily access the Benin Bronzes than the people of Nigeria?
Why are people who live within a day’s drive of London entitled to go and see the Elgin Marbles whenever they want, but the people of Athens aren’t?
What intrinsic factors make the West a suitable home for these artifacts but preclude them from being preserved and displayed by their countries of origin?
If your conclusion is that the West is better able to preserve these artifacts, think about why you’re assuming that to be true.
translations: (45) 朱莉娅 对于评论区中那些对文物从美国和英国城市移走并归还其原产国有着强烈感受的人，我会请你们考虑：为什么你认为美国人比尼日利亚人更有权轻松接触贝宁青铜器？
为什么住在伦敦一天车程内的人有权随时去看埃尔金大理石，而雅典人却不能？
什么内在因素使西方成为这些文物的合适家园，却阻止它们由原产国保存和展示？
如果你的结论是西方更能保存这些文物，想想你为什么假设这是真的。

sentences: A. It is clear that the countries of origin have never been compensated for the stolen artifacts.
B. It is a flawed line of reasoning to argue against returning artifacts to their countries of origin.
C. Museum visitors can still learn as much from artifacts’ copies after the originals are returned.
D. Reproductions, even if perfectly made, cannot take the place of the authentic objects.
E. The real value of artifacts can only be recognized in their countries of origin rather than anywhere else.
F. Ways to get artifacts from other countries must be decent and lawful.
G. Concern over security is no excuse for refusing to return artifacts to their countries of origin.
translations: A. 很明显，原产国从未因被盗文物得到补偿。
B. 反对将文物归还其原产国是一种有缺陷的推理。
C. 原件归还后，博物馆参观者仍然可以从文物复制品中学到同样多的东西。
D. 复制品，即使制作完美，也不能取代真实物品。
E. 文物的真正价值只能在其原产国被认可，而不是在其他任何地方。
F. 从其他国家获取文物的方式必须体面和合法。
G. 对安全的担忧不是拒绝将文物归还其原产国的借口。
